system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel (AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free)**

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A materially higher, negotiated cap reflecting the risk and recoverability of warranty claims; keep separate, higher treatment for fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims. | **Reject as drafted; seek a higher general cap.** A 20% cap may leave substantial losses unrecoverable, particularly given the identified risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a deductible basket (or, failing that, a lower tipping basket); exclude specific indemnities and fundamental claims from thresholds. | **Seek lower thresholds and a deductible basket.** The proposed tipping basket lets the Seller recover all claims only after the threshold, while excluding the first AUD 250,000 would materially dilute recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller proposes limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period, with separate longer periods for tax, title/fundamental and specific indemnity claims; no default extension of general limits to all Claims. | **Seek at least 24 months for general warranties and express separate periods.** 18 months may be too short to identify latent issues, and ambiguity could improperly shorten other claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limits. | Fundamental warranties uncapped or subject to a substantially higher cap, with a longer limitation period; title to shares should be covered expressly. | **Reject; carve fundamental and title claims out of the general regime.** Defects in ownership or authority undermine the transaction itself and warrant stronger protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions said to apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out in the update. | Expressly preserve claims for fraud and fraudulent concealment (including applicable attribution), and disapply caps, baskets, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance restrictions to the extent legally permitted. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** No contractual protection should shield fraud or restrict remedies for it. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room as at 22 September 2026, accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require a properly indexed, specific disclosure regime.** Blanket incorporation obscures what was disclosed and can defeat warranties without meaningful notice. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; at most, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry, with no waiver of fraud or specific indemnity claims. | **Reject the broad qualifier.** “Discoverable” knowledge makes the warranty package depend on hindsight and diligence scope rather than agreed risk allocation. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and conditions in clause 11.3; no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | Completion condition requiring final, unconditional consent and satisfaction/waiver of all conditions, with no material adverse amendment; Buyer termination right if not obtained. | **Make valid consent and condition satisfaction a condition precedent.** Bluefen concentration makes an ineffective or conditional consent a material continuity risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, lender payout and irrevocable release/discharge of debt, guarantees and security as a completion deliverable; no post-completion reliance on Seller. | **Require simultaneous payoff and documentary discharge at Completion.** A post-completion release leaves the Company exposed to debt and security after a debt-free/cash-free sale. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are “for Seller” and not separately itemised in funds flow; payroll tax, super and other on-costs unclear. | Fully quantify and fund bonuses and all on-costs in the completion mechanics, with Seller responsible for pre-Completion entitlements; prevent double counting in price or working capital. | **Resolve and deduct/fund the full cost in the funds flow.** An unprovided-for liability could transfer to Buyer despite the debt-free/cash-free basis. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 makes transfer conditional on every SOW3 fee being paid; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, without independent verification, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Specific indemnity for loss arising from failure to obtain ownership/usable rights, plus payment/assignment evidence and a completion deliverable securing all required IP rights. | **Expand the indemnity and require verified payment and assignment.** The disclosed open fee and unmet/uncertain transfer condition threaten access to project materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; scope, access and notification status remain unknown. | Pre-Completion investigation and complete evidence; specific indemnity for incident-related claims, remediation and notification costs; cooperation and no settlement/admission without Buyer consent. | **Do not accept a materiality dismissal; require investigation and specific protection.** The potential 1,240-record export creates unresolved privacy, regulatory and remediation exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (~AUD 330,000 aggregate) treated as ordinary-course costs. DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together; avoidability, termination, accrual and ordinary-course status are not established. | Confirm terms, timing, termination rights and whether committed/accrued; address any pre-Completion commitment or unusual liability through completion accounts, specific disclosure/protection or a condition as appropriate. | **Require evidence and quantify the committed exposure before agreeing treatment.** “Ordinary course” is asserted, not established, and the aggregate may affect value or post-close obligations. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and other claims, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies; preserve fraud carve-out. | **Reject a single all-Claims regime.** Different claim types warrant different protections, and the draft risks sweeping specific protections into inadequate general limits. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100% of issued shares. | Verify the register against the constitution, ASIC records and original share evidence; obtain title, capacity, no-encumbrance and valid-issue warranties and transfer deliverables. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive; verify and obtain express warranties.** The disclosure identifies the source relied on but does not establish independent verification or defect-free title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP settled under the general regime; no tailored terms are provided. | Negotiate express tax warranties and a tax indemnity with appropriate survival and cap; obtain comprehensive IP ownership, licensing, infringement and employee/contractor assignment warranties, with specific remedies for known gaps. | **Keep tax and IP open and negotiate tailored protections.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve the exposure, and the general cap/time limit may be inadequate for latent liabilities. |

The separate disclosure on the office lease and Mossvale does **not** establish that landlord or Mossvale consent is required merely because of the share sale; verify the underlying provisions rather than assume a consent condition.
=== END ADVICE ===
